stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A person pulls a crate along the floor with a rope tilted at angle $\alpha$ from the horizontal. Sweep all four sliders ($F$, $\alpha$, $d$, $\Delta t$) and watch how the work $W$ and power $P$ react. Notice what happens as $\alpha \to 90°$.
stages.concept: Work of a constant force: $W = F \cdot d \cdot \cos(\alpha)$. Only the projection of $F$ along the displacement does work — the vertical component is 'wasted'. Mean power: $P = W / \Delta t$. When $\alpha = 90°$, $\cos(\alpha) = 0$ and no work is done, no matter how strong the pull.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target power $P^{*}$ is displayed. Tune the four sliders so that the delivered mean power $P = W / \Delta t$ matches $P^{*}$. Many combinations of $(F, \alpha, d, \Delta t)$ produce the same $P$ — pick any that works.
stages.concept: $P^{*} = \dfrac{F \cdot d \cdot \cos(\alpha)}{\Delta t}$. Doubling $F$ or $d$ doubles $P$; doubling $\Delta t$ halves $P$; increasing $\alpha$ shrinks $\cos(\alpha)$ and cuts $P$. Try holding three sliders and moving the fourth to fine-tune.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The force diagram and live readouts are hidden. You are given a target work $W^{*}$ and a fixed distance $d^{*}$. Compute $F$ and $\alpha$ on paper so that $W = F \cdot d^{*} \cdot \cos(\alpha) = W^{*}$, then set the sliders (including $d = d^{*}$) and submit.
stages.concept: Inverse formula: $F \cdot \cos(\alpha) = \dfrac{W^{*}}{d^{*}}$. Many $(F, \alpha)$ pairs satisfy it. The simplest choice is $\alpha = 0°$, which gives $F = W^{*} / d^{*}$ directly. $\Delta t$ does not enter — it only affects power, not work.

labels.tip1: sweep every slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: tune F, α, d, Δt so that P = W/Δt hits the target
labels.tip3: compute F and α on paper first, then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: F·cos(α) = W*/d*. Try α = 0° first, then F = W*/d*.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Δt does not enter the work formula — set it anywhere. Only F, α, d matter for W.

1.1: Push F to the top and Δt to the bottom — power should spike.
1.2: Now sweep α from 0° to 90°. What happens to W near 90°?
1.3: Only the horizontal component F·cos(α) does work. The vertical part just lifts the rope.

2.1: Read the target on the right. Which slider changes P fastest for you right now?
2.2: Fix α at 0° and Δt at a round number, then tune F and d to reach P*.
2.3: Direct solve: pick d and α, then F = P*·Δt / (d·cos α).

3.1: Set d to the shown d* first — it is fixed. Then F and α are your two unknowns.
3.2: The simplest path: pick α = 0°, then F = W*/d* is a single division.
3.3: If you want a non-trivial α: F = W* / (d*·cos α). Pick α, plug in, read F.
